claims.text: Phase-field modeling can be used to control phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys.
Phase-field modeling controls phase evolution by simulating thermodynamic and kinetic parameters that influence phase transformations.
The initial Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloy is a multiphase system containing various constituent phases.
Temperature, composition, and processing conditions are key parameters for phase-field modeling of this alloy.
The intervention affects grain-boundary morphology and phase distribution.
Phase transformations and microstructure evolution can be simulated using first-principles calculations or computational modeling.
Optimization based on the modeling will produce a 20% relative increase in the volume fraction of the desired phase.
The baseline volume fraction of the desired phase is 50%.
The model prediction has a boundary of 10% deviation from the predicted volume fraction.
Model accuracy and alloy-system complexity may reduce the predictability of phase evolution.
The modeling predictions can be experimentally tested using microstructure characterization and phase analysis.
The hypothesis is falsified if the measured desired-phase volume fraction deviates by more than 15% from the predicted value.

contradictions.description: The boundary permits or specifies a 10% deviation, whereas the falsification rule uses a different threshold of more than 15%, leaving deviations between 10% and 15% inconsistently classified.
